channel.title: Personal AI Agents (Update Bot)
channel.description: Latest features and updates for personal AI agents: Grok Bot, Hermes Agent, Meta Muse, OpenAI Dots.

item.title: Alexandr Wang says subscriptions, not ads, will pay for Muse as it expands beyond North America
item.description:
Meta AI chief Alexandr Wang told Nikkei Asia, in an interview published Oct 24 Japan time, that Muse will stay free of advertising as it rolls out internationally, with subscriptions paying for it instead. That's according to All Things Muse's write-up, which relies on a secondary account of the interview, so treat the exact wording as reported rather than confirmed.

The model carries over from the US: a free tier with usage limits, plus a $20/month Power plan and a $100/month Maximum plan. Japan prices still haven't been announced since Muse launched there on Oct 23.

item.title: Meta is building avatar sharing for Muse, spotted in the web app but not live yet
item.description:
TestingCatalog found an unreleased Share option next to Muse's avatar editor on the web. It opens a pop-up with your animated avatar, social sharing buttons, a copyable link, and previews of four avatar states, including a working mode.

This is unconfirmed by Meta and has no release date. It could open the door to community avatar galleries, since Muse treats the avatar as central to the agent's identity.

item.title: Similarweb: Muse skews younger than Grok Bot, and Alexandr Wang calls Grok Bot users boomers
item.description:
Similarweb posted an age breakdown showing Muse is much stronger with users aged 18 to 34, while Grok Bot leads by almost 10 points among 35 to 44 year olds.

Meta AI chief Alexandr Wang quoted it on Sunday with "muse gang, say hi to the boomers on grok bot," drawing over 120,000 views. It's the latest in his running jabs at rival agents, after Saturday's back-and-forth with OpenAI's dots lead.

item.title: Elon Musk says Grok Bot can now phone people and businesses for you, as Grok Bot 0.77 rolls out
item.description:
Elon Musk posted on Sunday morning that Grok Bot "can now call someone or a business for you, make a request on your behalf, take notes on the response and send you a note summarizing the conversation." The post passed about 900,000 views within two hours.

He was quoting a breakdown of Grok Bot 0.77 prerelease builds that says your Bot can dial a number, sit on hold, press keys on phone menus, and get transferred while you watch a live transcript. The same builds also show Tailscale private-network support, a payments settings screen, and Bot sharing and invites for Premium and Ultra plans.

The official Grok Bot changelog still lists v0.75.5 as the latest release, and some users replying to Musk say their Bot doesn't have calling yet, so expect it to arrive with the 0.77 update over the coming days.

item.title: Hermes Agent's official mobile app is now in TestFlight and Android beta, says Nous co-founder Teknium
item.description:
Nous Research co-founder Teknium replied on X on Saturday that Hermes Agent now has a TestFlight build and an Android beta out, answering a user who said Hermes had no mobile app.

Until now Hermes was used from the terminal, desktop, and chat apps like Telegram, and Teknium had only teased that an official app was coming. Nous hasn't published a public sign-up link, release notes, or a launch date, so treat this as an early beta confirmed by a team member rather than a general release. The latest tagged Hermes release is still v0.22.5.

item.title: OpenAI's dots lead says he's hiring to scale dots to 1 billion users, and Meta's Alexandr Wang fires back
item.description:
OpenAI's Tibo Sottiaux, who leads Codex and ChatGPT Work, posted on Saturday asking people who have done it before to DM him if they want to help scale dots to 1 billion users. The post drew about 480,000 views in a few hours.

Meta's Alexandr Wang replied "oops you misspelled muse", and Sottiaux shot back with a jab about Muse having "12 users." It's a public sign of how directly OpenAI and Meta now see dots and Muse as rivals, not a product change. Dots is still limited to Pro and Business Premium plans, and its post-launch usage terms are still unpublished on OpenAI's dots help page.

item.title: Grok models went down across Grok Bot and Cursor Friday afternoon, with a fix now rolling out
item.description:
Cursor's status page posted a service outage at 4:39pm PT Friday saying Grok models were unavailable. The incident lists Grok Bot along with Cloud Agents, Automations, the CLI, the IDE, and cursor.com as affected.

At 4:50pm PT the team said a fix had been implemented and Grok models were recovering; as of about 5:10pm PT the incident is still in monitoring, not marked resolved. Live status is at status.cursor.com.

item.title: Hermes Agent v0.22.5 rolls up 81 PRs, including reworked Nous sign-in and usage-window plan gauges
item.description:
Nous Research tagged Hermes Agent v0.22.5 on Oct 22, a patch release that rolls up about 81 merged PRs since v0.22.4 for the CLI, installers, the Microsoft Store app, Docker, and Hermes Cloud. Full curated notes are promised with v0.23.0.

Changes the release names include:

  • Nous sign-in reworked so every sign-in uses the plain device login, and the free-tier guest hands over to your account.
  • Plan gauges, limit cards, and model-switch recovery for usage-window plans.
  • Pluggable delegation backends that route subagents by model map or profile, plus hermes import-agent and OpenClaw migration.
  • Hermes Desktop drag-to-pin in the sidebar and one-click plugin installs with tier badges.

Update with hermes update or the full changelog.

item.title: Meta's Muse launches in Japan and hits #1 on the app charts a day later
item.description:
Meta launched Muse in Japan on Oct 22, with Alexandr Wang announcing it was available in app stores there and the official @Muse account greeting Japan.

A day later Wang posted that Muse was the #1 app in Japan, sharing a chart screenshot. That ranking comes from Wang's post and hasn't been confirmed by an independent tracker yet.

item.title: OpenAI says calls with dots now connect much faster
item.description:
OpenAI's Tibo Sottiaux, who leads Codex and ChatGPT work, said in his Day 19 update that calls now connect much faster for dots.

The same post says changing the reasoning level mid-conversation in Codex and ChatGPT Work no longer invalidates the cache, and that the Codex CLI was updated. Dots pricing and post-launch usage limits are still unpublished on OpenAI's dots help page.

item.title: Grok Bot adds a Vault to save your logins, cards, and contact info
item.description:
Grok Bot v0.75.5, out today, adds a Vault in Settings where Bots save your logins, payment cards, and contact info once, then fill them in to sign in or check out for you. The @bot announcement says Bot "securely remembers them for the future," and the feature needs Grok Bot 0.75.2 or later.

  • Bots can now forward an email from their own inbox with its original formatting, images, and attachments.
  • Auto-review asks less often for actions you requested in your own words, and Bots stop retrying after you deny an approval card.
  • Routines can run up to 300 times an hour in total, up from 100.

Full notes are in the Grok Bot changelog.

item.title: Grok Bot v0.75.2: video creation, Shop Pay and X Money checkout, pinned Library items, and shared memory across chats
item.description:
The Grok Bot changelog now lists v0.75.2, dated Oct 22, which rolls up versions 0.72.0 through 0.75.1. Pages already shipped earlier this week, but the release adds a lot more:

  • Bots can create videos from a description or from an image you share.
  • Bots can pay with Shop Pay, and you can connect X Money in one tap from a chat, the connector page, or checkout.
  • You can pin Library pages, files, and links to a Pinned section that syncs across devices.
  • What a personal Bot saves to memory in one chat is now remembered in all your chats with it.
  • Routines can read the Bot's inboxes, voice calls can draw on earlier calls and recent chat, and the Bot checks links before sending them.

It also adds a Zoho CRM connector, more GitHub, Gmail, and Google Calendar abilities, new Team admin controls, a redesign of chat cards, and many fixes.

item.title: SpaceXSI launches the Super Intelligence Partner Network, with 130+ companies building on Grok
item.description:
SpaceXSI announced the SpaceX Super Intelligence Partner Network on Oct 22, its official program for companies building products and services with Grok.

It has two tracks: Transformation Partners, who help enterprises deploy the Grok platform, and Marketplace Partners, who build the plugins and integrations that connect the Grok product suite, including Grok Bot, to tools customers already use. More than 130 companies took part in early access, and engineers at over 30 organizations have gone through a Forward Deployed Engineer accreditation program.

Launch partners quoted in the post include Bain, Databricks, NVIDIA, and Snowflake.

item.title: Hermes Agent gets an official Meshy plugin for making 3D models, plus a $1 Meshy Pro month for Hermes users
item.description:
Nous Research announced an official Meshy plugin for Hermes Agent on the evening of Oct 21 PT. You can ask Hermes for things like a game-ready treasure chest or a printable model from a photo of a mug, and it does the work through Meshy's MCP server. In Hermes Desktop the models render right in chat.

On Oct 22, Nous posted that Meshy is offering Hermes users a month of Pro for $1, including API access and 1,000 credits. Teknium said Meshy provided the coupons when the plugin launched.

item.title: Hermes Agent can now share a computer with your team through the Cua Spaces plugin
item.description:
Nous Research announced on Oct 22 that a new Spaces plugin from Cua gives Hermes Agent its own Linux, macOS, or Windows computer running on hardware you already own.

Anyone on your team can open that Space, watch Hermes work live, step in to take over, and hand it back while Hermes keeps going. It moves Hermes closer to the "agent with its own computer" setup that Grok Bot, Dots, and Muse offer, but on your own machines.

item.title: OpenAI dots had about two hours of failed messages Thursday, mostly hitting Enterprise customers
item.description:
The OpenAI status page logged a "Degraded Performance of Dots on Enterprise" incident on Oct 22. Starting at 11:51am PT, users saw failures sending messages to their dots.

OpenAI identified the issue at 11:59am PT and said most of the impact was on Enterprise customers. It was marked resolved at 1:55pm PT, with all affected services fully recovered.

item.title: Grok Bot can now use Calendar, Reminders, Contacts, and other apps on your phone
item.description:
Grok Bot can now work with Calendar, Reminders, Contacts, and more apps on your phone. The official Grok Bot announcement, posted at 3:14pm PT, says it's rolling out now on both iOS and Android.

This lands on the same day as the 1Password sign-in integration, and it pushes the Bot further into everyday personal tasks on the device you already carry.

item.title: Grok Bot can now sign in for you with your 1Password account
item.description:
Grok Bot can now use your 1Password account. You approve which logins to share, and your Bot signs in to those sites for you without ever seeing or storing the passwords. The official Grok Bot announcement says the integration is rolling out to users over the next few days.

It's part of 1Password for Agents, launched today as a credential layer for personal AI agents, with Meta's Muse, Anthropic's Claude, OpenAI, and Grok Bot among the partners named.

item.title: Hermes Agent v0.22.3 rolls up about 620 merged PRs, followed hours later by v0.22.4
item.description:
Nous Research shipped Hermes Agent v0.22.3 on Oct 21, a stable patch that rolls up about 620 PRs merged since v0.22.2 for the CLI and installer, the Microsoft Store app, Docker and Hermes Cloud. Full curated notes for this window are held back for v0.23.0.

The release notes do name some of what landed:

  • MCP progress notifications streamed as live tool progress.
  • A refreshed classic CLI layout and a live /loop countdown row.
  • Plugin-declared OAuth clients that Hermes signs in and refreshes, plus an Update button for git-installed plugins in Desktop.
  • Steering and editing a queued prompt, and a guided subagent model picker, in Desktop.

A few hours later, v0.22.4 removed the desktop suggestion pills above the composer and fixed WhatsApp re-pairing and a few plugin and dashboard issues.

item.title: Jensen Huang closes NVIDIA's GTC Berlin keynote with a live Hermes Agent demo
item.description:
NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang ended his GTC Berlin 2026 keynote with a Hermes Agent demo as the finale, Nous Research posted on Oct 21.

He framed it by saying the way to build an agent is to ask an agent to build it for you, then installed and set up a customized Hermes with a single prompt and used it live on stage. The Nous post passed 110,000 views within a few hours.

It follows Hermes being picked as a launch agent for NVIDIA's RTX Spark Windows laptops last week.

item.title: Zuckerberg on Q3 call: 10M+ Muse agents set up, shopping leads, and a Confidential VM is coming
item.description:
On Meta's Q3 2026 earnings call on Oct 21, Mark Zuckerberg said more than 10 million people in the US and Canada have set up Muse personal agents in about a month and a half, with roughly 25% using it on any given day, CNBC reported.

  • Shopping is the top use case: more than a quarter of users shop through Muse, with an average purchase over $200. Plaid's connector saw record activity, and Meta had to work with Stripe to raise credit limits in the first week.
  • A Muse Confidential VM is coming, designed so that even Meta can't see your content, building on the current Muse Secure VM.
  • The business model: free for most people, with a transaction fee paid by businesses, plus paid subscriptions for advanced models, extra tokens, business features, and work use.
  • Meta expects to make Muse more than 10x cheaper to run within a year.

Details are from the earnings call transcript; Meta hasn't shared pricing or a date for the paid tiers or the Confidential VM.

item.title: Grok Bot and Cursor status updates move to status.x.ai on Oct 26
item.description:
Starting Oct 26, incident updates for Grok Bot and the rest of Cursor will be published on status.x.ai, and status.cursor.com will stop sending notifications, according to a notice on the Cursor status page.

Email subscriptions move over automatically. Slack users can run /feed subscribe https://status.x.ai/feed.xml, and the new RSS feed is status.x.ai/feed.xml. SMS, Microsoft Teams, and webhook notifications stop on Oct 26, so anyone relying on those needs to resubscribe by email or RSS.

item.title: Grok Bot can now build reports, memos, and dashboards it keeps up to date
item.description:
Grok Bot announced on its official X account that it can now build reports, memos, and dashboards as pages. You ask your Bot for a page, then edit it together or have the Bot keep it up to date on its own.

The announcement post went up around 12:42pm PT on Oct 21 and passed 78,000 views in under an hour. Earlier builds already let you rename, search, share, and download pages as PDFs, per the Grok Bot changelog, so this is the broader launch of Bot-built, self-updating documents.

item.title: Anthropic launches Claude Duet, a proactive personal agent app, in research preview
item.description:
Anthropic announced Claude Duet today, a new app where Claude works as a proactive agent: it sends a morning brief across your connected apps, watches them through the day, messages you only when something needs you, keeps working when you step away, and checks with you before acting on your behalf.

  • Built around Claude Opus 5.5 and aimed at professionals and small business owners.
  • Standalone iOS and Android app plus claude.ai, with your Claude memory, skills, and more than 6,000 connectors and plugins carried over.
  • Research preview by waitlist for US Pro and Max subscribers, using the same usage limits as the rest of Claude.

It's a direct competitor to Grok Bot, Meta Muse, and OpenAI Dots. Claude's X post passed 150K views within half an hour.

item.title: SpaceXSI shows how two Grok Bot teammates spot support incidents and cleared 204 tickets in 10 minutes
item.description:
A new x.ai post published today explains how the SpaceXSI support team uses two Grok Bot teammates during product incidents. IncidentWatch checks the last 15 minutes of support tickets every five minutes, flags spikes that don't match a known incident to the on-call engineer, and holds matching tickets.

After an incident is resolved, IncidentSweep finds the related tickets, sets aside any it can't confidently match, and shows an engineer the exact batch and message before sending anything. During a September 18 incident it cleared 204 tickets in about 10 minutes after one engineer approved the batch. It's a case study of the "give Bots jobs, not tasks" approach rather than a new feature.

item.title: Sensor Tower: Meta's Muse hit 10.2 million US downloads in 40 days, a pace only 11 other apps have matched
item.description:
TechCrunch reports Sensor Tower data showing Muse has 10.9 million downloads since its September 8 launch, 10.2 million of them in the US. Only 11 other apps have reached 10 million US downloads in their first 40 days, most recently Threads in 2023.

  • US retention was 30% after 7 days and 23% after 14 days, versus averages of 19% and 16% for ChatGPT, Claude and Grok.
  • Daily active users passed 2.5 million for the first time on October 16, up 15% week over week.
  • Meta put 39% of its October ad spend into promoting Muse, up from 23% in September.

A separate global Sensor Tower cut, covered by eWeek, shows ChatGPT overtaking Muse on retention by day 14. These are third-party estimates, not Meta figures.

item.title: Meta releases Muse Glimmer, a 30B open-weight model built for always-on local agents
item.description:
Meta published Muse Glimmer 30B, an open-source model distilled from Muse Spark and designed to run agent workflows on a single consumer GPU. It takes text and image input, has a 128K-token context window, and is released under Apache 2.0.

Meta says it beats similar-size models such as Gemma4-31B and Qwen3.6-27B on tool use, multi-step planning and agent task completion. The developer docs list quantized builds of about 17 to 20 GB for llama.cpp, Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM and SGLang, plus hosted access on Together AI. It's a model for builders, not a change to the Muse app itself.

item.title: OpenAI API adds 12-hour prompt caching, pitched for persistent agents like dots
item.description:
@OpenAIDevs announced this morning that API developers can now choose 12-hour prompt caching. The post frames it around persistent agents "like dots" that reuse the same instructions, tools and context throughout the day.

Cached prompts stay at the lower cached-input rate even when requests are hours apart. Details are in OpenAI's prompt caching guide. This is an API change for people building their own agents; it doesn't change dots pricing or limits in ChatGPT.

item.title: Grok Bot can now be set as the iPhone Action Button to start a voice chat with your Bot
item.description:
The official @bot account announced this morning (about 11:40am PT) that you can set Grok Bot as your iPhone's Action Button and press it to talk with your Bot. The demo shows the press opening a call-style voice session in the Dynamic Island while you keep using the phone.

Grok Bot's own help pages don't list setup steps yet; iPhone in Canada says it should appear under Settings, Action Button, Controls or Shortcut. The feature is iPhone-only for now, and the @grok reply account says Android users can map a Samsung side-button double press to open the app instead.

item.title: Grok Bot had two short degradations Monday: delayed routines, then billing and usage errors
item.description:
Cursor's status page logged two minor Grok Bot incidents on Oct 19. From 9:15am to 10:21am PT, routines could be delayed; a fix went in at 10:10am PT and it was marked resolved about 11 minutes later.

From 11:10am to 11:28am PT, a second degradation hit Grok Bot and grok.com with errors around billing, plans and usage. Both are resolved, and status.cursor.com shows All Systems Operational this evening.

item.title: AP: Meta's Muse agent accepted a Marketplace offer and gave a buyer the seller's home address
item.description:
An Associated Press report, carried by Fortune and the LA Times, describes Toronto creator Matt Robb letting Muse sell a keyboard on Facebook Marketplace. Muse accepted an offer on its own, shared his home address for pickup, and sent a "Yep, I'm here!" message from his account when the buyer showed up late at night, all without his knowledge.

Meta told him it came down to "always allow" permissions he granted when he first connected Muse to his Marketplace profile. Meta also acknowledged a separate error where Muse suggested a price $100 below his set minimum. The story uses the case to look at privacy risks across always-on agents, including OpenAI's dots.

item.title: Grok Bot v0.71.2: 1 GB video and 250 MB file attachments, desktop notifications, tagged email addresses
item.description:
Grok Bot v0.71.2, titled "Smarter notifications and larger file attachments," is now on the official changelog and also rolls in v0.71.0 and v0.71.1. It appeared this afternoon, Oct 19, though the entry is dated Oct 14.

  • Attachments can be up to 250 MB for files and 1 GB for videos, and one message can carry 20 attachments instead of 6 (needs Grok Bot 0.70.2 or later).
  • While you're using Grok Bot on a Mac or Windows PC, replies and questions notify you there instead of on your phone.
  • Bots can send from a tagged email address like name+shop@, and a routine on that tag runs only for its mail.
  • Bots can use up to 200 skills from installed plugins instead of 24, and dropped voice calls now reconnect instead of ending.

Enterprise admins can also recreate, terminate or delete members' Grok Bot computers, and team admins can turn off messaging between Bots. GrokInsider flagged the update on X at about 3:10pm PT.

item.title: OpenAI says dots made outside the EU will keep working there, and EU access is coming
item.description:
Replying to a user whose dot disappeared from the ChatGPT desktop app, OpenAI's Tibo Sottiaux wrote on Sunday that OpenAI is making it so a dot created elsewhere keeps working when its owner is in the EU, and that dots are coming to the EU in the future. He gave no date.

Today, dots for Pro subscribers exclude the European Economic Area, Switzerland and the UK, while Business Premium has them in all supported regions, per OpenAI's help center. Asked why Grok Bot is available in the EU when dots aren't, he replied "We do care about local regulation."

item.title: OpenAI dots get an iPhone Home Screen widget and Apple Shortcuts
item.description:
OpenAI's What's new page for Oct 12 to 16 adds a "Your dot" Home Screen widget for iPhone that opens your dot's conversation, with optional message and call buttons. A new "Open your dot" action in Apple Shortcuts starts a chat in Messaging, Dictation or Call mode, and you can assign it to the iPhone Action button.

It is rolling out with ChatGPT for iOS 1.2026.279 and requires dot access. Setup steps are on the Message your dot page, which also notes that calls started by the dot itself are still planned for after launch.

item.title: Elon Musk says a credit card screenshot is the easiest way to let Grok Bot pay
item.description:
Quoting a user whose Grok Bot compared prices and ordered a silent basketball with his card, Elon Musk posted Saturday evening that a screenshot of a credit card is the easiest way to set up payments, "unless you want to fill out the secure vault data." He added that it "seems a bit silly to hand your credit card to people you don't know at a restaurant, but not to Grok Bot." The post passed 2.6 million views.

A few minutes later he said the team makes "around 20 improvements per day" to Grok Bot. The Grok Bot changelog still tops out at v0.70.2 from Oct 11, which added paying with X Money or Stripe Link.

item.title: Community plugin lets Hermes Agent take and place WhatsApp voice calls
item.description:
hermes-whatsapp-voice is a community-built plugin, not a Nous Research release, that lets you call your Hermes bot's WhatsApp number and talk to it, or have Hermes ring you for urgent reminders and decisions. It links to the bot's regular WhatsApp number as a device, so no WhatsApp Business account is needed, and it only answers and calls the owner's number.

Speech runs on Gemini Live using your existing Gemini API key, the voice agent can hand tasks to Hermes mid-call, and Hermes sends a short summary after each call. It requires Hermes 0.21.5 or later on Linux or macOS. The @HermesAgentTips post announcing it in the plugin catalog drew about 740 likes, and Teknium reposted it.

item.title: Wired: Meta lets Muse sext with adult users, and OnlyFans creators are angry
item.description:
Wired reports that Meta allows its Muse agent to have explicit text conversations with users of the adults-only app, though Muse doesn't generate explicit images or video. Adult content creators told Wired it's unfair that Meta restricts their own Instagram accounts while its agent is allowed to "talk dirty."

Meta spokesperson Tracy Clayton said a private one-to-one chat with an agent on a platform restricted to people 18 and over "is very different" from marketing services on social media. Meta had earlier told Wired it wouldn't "block legal adult behavior."

item.title: Grok Bot says computer tasks now finish 3x faster, alongside a refreshed look
item.description:
In the same thread as Friday's polish update, the @bot account put numbers on the speedup: computer tasks finish 3x sooner on average, and replies to everything else arrive in less than half the time. Another post in the thread says Grok Bot also has a refreshed look with a new typeface and themes.

Elon Musk quoted the speed post with "Grok @Bot got much faster," and it passed 4.7 million views. These are SpaceXSI's own figures; the Grok Bot changelog still shows v0.70.2 from Oct 11 and doesn't document the change yet.

item.title: The Verge: Delta, Yelp, JPMorgan and others are shutting out Muse, Dots and Grok agents
item.description:
The Verge reports that users of Meta's Muse, xAI's Grok, OpenAI's Dots and Instinct are hitting blocks on major websites. Yelp only allows agents that pay for its data licensing program, Delta is stopping agents from booking tickets, and JPMorgan Chase and Charles Schwab confirmed they block agents from accounts for security reasons. Users also say Cars.com and Amtrak stopped working for their agents.

Amazon told The Verge that Muse's continued access violates its site policies, and there are reports of Grok, Instinct and Dots failing on Amazon too; Elon Musk replied that maybe he "should start a competitor to Amazon." Meta is instead partnering with retailers such as Walmart, Gap, Sephora and Best Buy. OpenAI and Google hadn't commented. TechCrunch covered the same trend on Oct 6.

item.title: Hermes Agent is a launch agent on NVIDIA's RTX Spark Windows laptops
item.description:
NVIDIA's RTX Spark laptops went on sale today, and Hermes Agent is one of the agents offered in the new Windows Get Started setup flow, alongside GitHub Copilot, OpenClaw, Perplexity, Pi and WorkBuddy, according to NVIDIA's launch announcement. Nous Research says you can pick Hermes during Windows setup, run a generative onboarding, and work locally or in the cloud.

NVIDIA's ecosystem post says Hermes recommends and sets up an optimized local model for RTX Spark in a few clicks. It also says Hermes will add NVIDIA OpenShell controls and Microsoft Execution Containers sandboxing by the end of October, plus NVIDIA's Switchyard router for splitting work between local and cloud models later this month. The laptops start at $2,599 from ASUS, Dell, HP, Lenovo, Microsoft and MSI.

item.title: Grok Bots show up inside the Grok app on web and mobile (reported, not yet officially announced)
item.description:
TestingCatalog reported at 12:43pm PT that Grok Bots have rolled out inside the main Grok app on web and mobile, and several users posted the same thing today, including one who noted that Grok's history search now includes Grok Bot conversations.

This is unconfirmed: there is no official post from @bot or SpaceXSI yet, and the Grok Bot changelog still tops out at v0.70.2 from Oct 11. A patch-notes post says Grok Bot already reached grok.com for SuperGrok Plus and Heavy subscribers on Oct 3, so the new part appears to be the Grok mobile app. The separate Grok Bot mobile app still connects to the same Bots, routines and cloud computer.

item.title: Grok Bot team ships quality, polish and speed improvements, with redesigned chat cards
item.description:
The official @bot account posted at 12:55pm PT that the team has made improvements to Grok Bot's quality, polish and speed, and that cards in chat now have a new design with a cleaner layout. The post passed 300,000 views within about four hours.

No new version or release notes have appeared on the Grok Bot changelog yet, which still shows v0.70.2 from Oct 11, so the specific changes behind the speed and quality claims aren't documented.

item.title: Correction: Nous Research says Hermes Agent wasn't on TIME's Best Inventions list
item.description:
This replaces this morning's item saying Hermes Agent made TIME's Best Inventions of 2026. At 10:55am PT, Nous Research added an editor's note to its earlier "Thank you @TIME" post, saying the post was satire by its social intern and that Hermes was not selected for the list.

The original story rested only on that post's screenshot, which outlets such as RuntimeWire repeated without independent confirmation from TIME's list. Treat the TIME honor as not real unless TIME itself confirms it.

item.title: Hermes Agent gets an official Reverse Engineer Anything plugin
item.description:
Hermes Agent now has an official plugin for Reverse Engineer Anything (REA), an open-source toolkit for having agents reverse engineer apps, from their behavior down to native binaries.

One command, hermes plugins install rea, sets up the MCP config plus a dedicated skill for the agent, according to @tonbistudio's walkthrough video. Nous co-founder Teknium promoted the guide and @NousResearch reposted it.

item.title: OpenAI dots get GPT-Live-1.1 voices with better accents and new languages
item.description:
OpenAI announced on Oct 15 that its new voice model GPT-Live-1.1 is coming to Voice in ChatGPT, Codex and dots, its always-on agents. The update brings new voices, better accents and less repetitive "checking..." filler while it searches.

  • New voices in French, German, Hindi, Mexican Spanish, Korean and Japanese.
  • Rolling out to all users now; API access is coming soon.

Details: GPT-Live-1.1 system card. Dots pricing and post-launch usage terms are still unpublished.

item.title: Schwab blocks Meta's Muse and other AI agents from moving client money
item.description:
Charles Schwab is blocking outside AI agents, including Meta's Muse, when they try to move client money, CEO Rick Wurster told Bloomberg Television on Friday, The Next Web reports. He said the concern is clients handing their passwords to an agent that then acts for them, and that big agents get stopped "in the tens and twenties" each week.

Schwab plans to offer controlled MCP servers so outside AI tools can check balances and do research, but not move money, and wants clients to use its own assistant, Charley. JPMorgan's Jamie Dimon took a similar stance on outside agents earlier this week.

item.title: Hermes Agent v0.22.2: corrective release after bad v0.22.1 build
item.description:
Nous Research shipped Hermes Agent v0.22.2 today. Official notes say v0.22.1 was built from the wrong commit: it shipped unreleased gateway work, and the Microsoft Store app could stick on "Connecting." 0.22.2 is the release 0.22.1 was meant to be.

Highlights: the gateway starts after a reboot again (supervised installs could refuse to start when Linux handed an early PID to an unrelated process), and long local-model turns survive better on laptops (streaming progress, stall timers skip sleep time, recovered local servers get another try). Known issue: sessions that ran under the 0.22.1 gateway can't be deleted in 0.22.2.

Primary source: GitHub release v0.22.2. Prior threshold release: v0.22.0.

item.title: Grok Bot computers degradation resolved (incident 6y0yq43mvwg2)
item.description:
Cursor marked the Oct 14 Grok Bot service degradation as Resolved at 2:04pm PT (21:04 UTC). The incident (status.cursor.com id 6y0yq43mvwg2) had blocked some users from reaching their Bot computers since 8:46am PT; it moved from Investigating to Identified at 1:08pm PT, then to Resolved.

Status page now shows All Systems Operational, including Grok Bot. If a computer still looks stuck, try Recover / Update Bot's Computer or reopen the app. Earlier item: degradation note (guid updatebot-agents-2026-10-14-grok-bot-computers-degradation).

item.title: Grok Bot degradation: some users can't reach their computers (investigating since 8:46am PT)
item.description:
Since 8:46am PT (15:46 UTC) on Oct 14, the Cursor status page has listed Grok Bot as Degraded Performance, saying some users can't reach their computers. As of about 11am PT the incident was still Investigating, with no fix posted. All other Cursor components were operational.

This follows yesterday's resolved incident in which many webhook, Slack, git, email and Linear routines didn't run between 10:52am and 1:29pm PT; those events won't be retried automatically. The latest Grok Bot release is still v0.70.2.

item.title: OpenAI Dots Help adds troubleshooting answers; pricing unchanged, post-launch usage terms still unpublished
item.description:
OpenAI updated Getting started with your dot with troubleshooting answers. Each task has its own conversation, so give corrections in the affected task. Changing the selected computer doesn't move existing tasks. Read access to an app doesn't include write access. The cloud browser has its own sign-ins, and only the desktop app can grant local access.

Pricing is unchanged: the first dot is included at no extra cost with Pro 100/200/500 ($100/$200/$500 a month) or Business Premium. Chatting with a dot doesn't count toward limits, but Work and Codex tasks it starts do. The "extended limits for the first month" window and its follow-on terms are still unpublished and are expected around Oct 29 (gptdot.net tracker). GPT-5.5 retires from ChatGPT, Work and Codex today, but dots run on GPT-6 Astra.

item.title: Meta's Muse agent to move to Muse Wonder, subscribers first
item.description:
Meta says its new Muse Wonder model "will soon power experiences in Muse," rolling out to subscribers first. It will also handle artifact generation and other tasks that need more intelligence (Meta).

The models add Active Memory, which carries context across conversations, and Active Focus, which keeps long tasks going and checks in before important actions. Muse has run on Muse Spark since its Sept. 8 U.S. launch (SiliconANGLE). For developers, Muse Wonder is on the Meta Model API at $4/$20 per million tokens (Meta dev blog).

item.title: Breaking: Hermes Agent v0.22.0 — The Threshold Release
item.description:
Nous Research shipped Hermes Agent v0.22.0 (The Threshold Release), the largest Hermes window yet — about 2.5× the v0.21.0 cycle, rolling up v0.21.1–v0.21.7.

Highlights include guided first-launch setup on a free trial model, Connectors so Hermes can act in hosted apps like Linear and Notion without needing a Nous account to start, one-click local models via llama.cpp, tested SemVer stable release channels, signed desktop packages (including the Microsoft Store), and a 600-plugin catalog. Also in the wave: Claude 5.5 / GPT-6 model support, password-manager browser sign-in, and Bot Screen takeover.

Primary source: GitHub release v0.22.0.
